title: Can I SURVIVE MORE Drawback Chess?
summary: Drawback Chess vs online humans; goal 5 wins, achieved in 6 games (5-1). G1 (black) Leveling Up vs opp Gloomstalker - W; G2 (drawback: can't move a piece further from the enemy king than it started) vs opp Forward March - L; G3 Spice of Life vs opp Stage Fright - W; G4 Winds of Fate vs opp Punching Down - W; G5 (black) Cowardly vs opp Boastful - W; G6 (black) Simon Says vs opp The Scent of Blood - W.
rules: Standard setup and moves; each player is dealt one secret random drawback (card with Easy-Hard difficulty slider); the opponent's drawback is revealed when the game ends ('Your opponent's drawback was ...').
No check/checkmate: kings may move into or stay in attack; capturing the enemy king wins.
Breaking or failing your drawback condition makes you lose (or the move is simply illegal, depending on drawback wording).
Players may chat/rename to bluff or reveal drawbacks.

Drawbacks in this video: Leveling Up - you can't capture a piece until you've captured its predecessor in the piece-value list (pawn -> knight/bishop -> rook -> queen). Gloomstalker - (text not read). (G2, name not read) - you can't make moves that place the moving piece further away from your opponent's king than it started. Forward March - (text not read). Spice of Life - you can't move the same piece type twice in a row. Stage Fright - you can't move to the center four squares. Winds of Fate - (text not read). Punching Down - (text not read). Cowardly - when your opponent captures, you must move backwards or lose. Boastful - you lose if you have fewer pieces than your opponent. Simon Says - you must move onto the same colour square as your opponent's last move. The Scent of Blood - you can't make non-capturing moves with pieces that could capture.
win_condition: Capture the enemy king. Goal: 5 wins.
